verdictStatement: Both v10 blockers were the same defect seen from two angles — a live-normative clause still routing terminalizers into a byte-set the artifact had deleted — and v11 fixes it in the one place it lived, with the surrounding design untouched. The new clause states the reserved-marker rule in capacityPause's own terms and adds 'There is no external pending-terminalizer record', so the two live capacity clauses now agree rather than contradict. I re-ran the removed-identifier sweep I recommended at v10 and it returns clean: pendingTerminalizerRecord has eight references and ZERO of them are live-normative — every survivor is in succession history, the append-only guidance list, or a folding note. I also ran a generic dangling-cross-reference sweep over every 'lifecycle.X' and 'terminalization.X' pointer in the artifact and found none unresolved. Codex's foldingNotes item is repaired past what it asked: the note advances to the v10 finding set and marks the v8 sentence historical rather than only doing one. The roster is the tightest of the lineage — it names the single leaf path that changed — and holds mechanically at 31 changed paths, zero off-roster, 319 of 319 non-roster paths byte-identical. I re-derived the structural elements from scratch rather than carrying them forward on trust: row verbatim, the 13-line carry, all six governing digests, the manifest field list, the four negative tests, the G19 standing, the placement standings, and the FC-RO residue count all check out independently. I found nothing to raise at any severity.

coordinatorNote: ACCEPT, and I want to be exact about what I am accepting. This is a candidate artifact that binds nothing: DR-124 stays OPEN, SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL stays PROPOSED with seven owner roles' concurrence outstanding and D-096 (A) unsatisfied as of D-100, no DR is SATISFIED, nothing is QUALIFIED, and docs/v2/implementation/ is not authorized. My ACCEPT supplies none of those and mints nothing. On the merits: v11 repairs the only two findings from the v10 round, which were one defect seen twice, and it does so in the single leaf path the roster names, leaving the surrounding design byte-identical. I looked hard for a reason to hold it — I re-ran the removed-identifier sweep, widened it to every cross-reference pointer in the artifact, re-derived the row, the carry, the six digests, the manifest fields, the negative tests, the G19 standing, the placement standings and the FC-RO residue from the live sources rather than carrying any of them forward on trust, and re-tested my own v9-era reasoning about whyNotSilent. Nothing survived at any severity, so the 0-and-0 gate is met on measurement rather than on the absence of effort. Two things worth carrying to disposition: the artifact's substantive architecture has been stable since v4 and every finding since has been bookkeeping, which is the shape you would expect of a contract that is ready; and the identifier sweep at OBS-2 is worth generalising, since it turns the one class of defect that reached a blocker at v10 into a mechanical check. I did not read the other current v11 reviewer, did not edit the subject or the prompt, did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not apply SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, did not mark any DR SATISFIED, and did not commit.
